claim: For the Ding–Ding flow \(\dot x=a(y-x),\;\dot y=bx-y-xz+w,\;\dot z=x^2-cz,\;\dot w=w-dx^3\) with \(a,b,c,d>0\), the complete real equilibrium set is as follows. If \(dc\ne1\), put \(R=c(1-b)/(dc-1)\): for \(R>0\) there are exactly the origin and \(E_\pm=(\pm\sqrt R,\pm\sqrt R,R/c,\pm dR^{3/2})\), while for \(R\le0\) the origin is the only equilibrium. If \(dc=1\), the origin is the only equilibrium when \(b\ne1\), whereas for \(b=1\) the full curve \(\{(x,x,x^2/c,x^3/c):x\in\mathbb R\}\) consists of equilibria. At the source parameters \((a,b,c,d)=(24,25,3,1/2)\), \(R=-144\), so the origin is the only equilibrium and the displayed red curve is not an equilibrium set. Moreover, the origin always has the exact eigenvalue \(1\), hence is linearly unstable. Therefore the source's generic equilibrium-curve assertion and its arbitrary-parameter-on-the-curve local-stability calculation do not apply to the printed differential equations except on the stated equilibrium locus; this correction does not by itself negate the separately simulated hyperchaotic trajectories or image-encryption experiments.
integrity: The classification follows by exact substitution into the printed polynomial vector field and an exhaustive case split on \(dc=1\) and the sign of the resulting square. The packaged script is supporting replay, not a substitute for the proof.
scientific_limitations: The result classifies equilibria and corrects the applicability of the local-stability calculation. It does not disprove the numerically simulated hyperchaotic trajectories, recompute their Lyapunov exponents, or assess the encryption experiments.
title: Complete equilibrium diagram of the Ding–Ding four-dimensional flow
